title: Read the community files
summary: Community files help people use and contribute to a repository. A licence explains reuse conditions; other files describe participation and reporting.
introduction: Community files help people use and contribute to a repository. A licence explains reuse conditions; other files describe participation and reporting. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: Community files help people use and contribute to a repository. A licence explains reuse conditions; other files describe participation and reporting.

blocks.code:
README.md: purpose and setup
LICENSE: reuse conditions
CONTRIBUTING.md: how to propose a change
CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md: community behaviour
SECURITY.md: how to report a security issue if provided
blocks.title: Read the community files

blocks.text: These files answer different questions. Read the security reporting instructions before posting sensitive vulnerability details publicly.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Choose which file answers whether you may reuse project code.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Public visibility alone does not mean code has no reuse conditions.
For more detail later, use this [GitHub further reading](https://docs.github.com/en/get-started).
